The wordplay is on “courses.” The student is not choosing academic classes at HKU. Instead, the “courses” are the dishes/courses of a hall dinner—a high-table dinner associated with the student’s hall. The student had to choose/arrange the menu courses before a deadline for that dinner. The dinner then took place that same evening: the chosen courses were served to the diners and cleared away course by course as the meal progressed. By the end of that one evening, all the selected “courses” had been eaten and cleared away—so “all of my courses were gone in one evening.” The apparent academic-course-selection problem is thus a pun: the courses were meal courses, and they disappeared because the hall dinner was served and cleared that night.
